correctness.rationale: One-sided purchaser sets force one complete part and have n purchasers. Mixed sets have p,q >=1 and exactly the four tight degree/coverage inequalities; explicit modular nominations establish sufficiency, and balanced p,q reduce the problem to a monotone integer condition. The even/odd threshold and exceptional k=n case yield the exact formula with quantified n>=2,1<=k<=n. Direct exact-subset verifier passes all 35 pairs through n=8; infinite proof independent of these tests.

originality.rationale: A full-text comparison with Gerke et al. 2019/2023 (Definition 3, Theorem 1, Theorem 2, Appendix C) establishes only general extrema bounds and complete-graph sharp results, not the exact K_{n,n} equilibrium purchaser-count spectrum. Gutin–Neary–Yeo (2020/2023) treats uniqueness complexity. Deligkas et al. (2025) already covers an implication about minimum buyers for capacity one; this is explicitly excluded as an independent novelty claim. Direct mathematical comparison with the closest publicly indexed biclique packing and limited-domination theorems shows genuinely different constraints. No covering statement was located in actual focused searches or recoverable prior research claims; the unindexed-literature risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: A less-indexed study may derive the same all-capacity K_{n,n} D-set spectrum using exact capacitated domination terminology or equilibrium-support terminology.
Source-derived DP-Nash correspondence applies to specialised equilibria; a statement about arbitrary nonspecialised pure strategies is not asserted.

value.rationale: Computes the complete natural equilibrium purchaser-count spectrum, including unattainable interior counts, not merely minimum and maximum. Produces arbitrarily long gaps and a sharp purchasing-cost reversal from 2 to n on regular K_{n,n} when capacity rises by one. These determine genuinely different equilibrium participation burdens and quantify a structural phenomenon beyond earlier particular-network examples.
